title: 1.5.23 Spot the Broken Pseudocode
description: A plan that never finishes, found by reading rather than running. Diagnose it and rewrite it — in pseudocode, not code. AI-graded with hints.

aiGrader.rubricTitle: Spot the Broken Pseudocode — AI-graded rubric
aiGrader.prompt:
Here is somebody's plan. It has no syntax errors, because pseudocode has no syntax. It is still wrong.

  set count to 1
  while count is less than 10
      print count

1. What is wrong with it? Read it back literally, one line at a time, and say what makes the loop never finish.

2. Rewrite the plan correctly, in pseudocode. Use indentation to show which steps are inside the loop. Do not write JavaScript - no braces, no semicolons.

3. Which line in your corrected plan is the one that guarantees it ends, and why does it guarantee that?

4. This plan was caught by reading it aloud rather than by running it. Why would running it have been a worse way to find this particular problem?

rubric.title: Q1: identifies that count never changes
rubric.description: Student says nothing ever increases count, so the condition stays true and the plan repeats forever. Credit any wording that identifies the unchanging variable as the cause - 'count is always 1', 'nothing updates it', 'the condition can never become false'. Deny answers that blame the print statement, the starting value, or the number 10.

rubric.title: Q2: the rewritten plan adds the missing step
rubric.description: The corrected pseudocode includes a step that increases count inside the loop - 'add 1 to count' or equivalent. Deny if the rewrite only reorders or reworks the existing three lines without adding a step that changes count.

rubric.title: Q2: indentation shows what is inside the loop
rubric.description: The steps that repeat are indented under the while line, and anything that happens once is not. Deny if everything is flush left, or if the indentation does not correspond to what belongs inside the loop.

rubric.title: Q2: the answer is pseudocode, not JavaScript
rubric.description: The rewrite reads as plain structured English. Keywords such as WHILE or IF are fine. Deny if the student submits real JavaScript with braces, semicolons and console.log - the point of the exercise is that this stage has no language.

rubric.title: Q3: names the line that guarantees termination, and why
rubric.description: Student points at the step that increases count and explains that because count grows on every pass, it must eventually reach 10 and fail the condition. Credit any clear statement of that mechanism. Deny if a line is named with no reasoning, or the wrong line is named.

rubric.title: Q4: says why reading beat running here
rubric.description: Student recognises that running this would hang or loop forever rather than report a useful error, so it would tell you little about the cause - whereas reading it exposes the missing step directly. Credit any answer along those lines, including 'it would never stop so you'd learn nothing' or 'there is no error message for a plan that is simply wrong'.
